summary: Verified both shipped changes end-to-end: (1) backend admin profile endpoints GET /api/admin/me and POST /api/admin/me/credentials with all validation paths; (2) frontend Admin Panel 'Профиль' tab with all data-testids functional; (3) CSS padding-bottom: 85px applied to .bottom-sheet.with-fabbar. Admin credentials restored to admin@taxi.local/admin123 at end of testing. test_credentials.md sync verified — and reset to original after tests.

integration_issues.issue: Frontend caches initial user.email from /admin/me at mount and uses it to decide wantEmailChange. After a successful email change the FE state res.email is set as new_email but user.email cached state is NOT refreshed — so attempting to immediately submit a SECOND change that 'restores' to the originally-loaded value is silently blocked by the FE guard with msg 'Измените email или пароль'. Backend still has the changed email. Fix: refresh user via loadMe() after successful credentials update, or rely solely on backend validation.

action_items: After a successful POST /admin/me/credentials, also reload the admin user state in AdminPanel (e.g., call /admin/me) so subsequent email/password edits from the SAME session correctly detect new vs current email. Currently the FE guard uses stale user?.email and prevents restore-style edits without a page reload.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:1424-1432 — email collision check correctly excludes current user by id. Good.

server.py:1444-1458 — test_credentials.md is rewritten on every successful credentials update. When ONLY email changes (no new_password) the file records 'Password: (unchanged)' instead of the actual current password. This is misleading for next testing agents and could break automated test fixtures. Suggestion: persist the last-known plaintext or omit the password line when unchanged AND warn, or better, keep the file authoritative by not overwriting the password line when not changed (leave previous content intact). Currently the agent had to manually restore the file. LOW priority but worth fixing.

AdminPanel.js handleSaveCredentials does not call loadMe() after success → causes 'restore email' UX issue described above. Recommended fix is small: after success refetch user via /admin/me and update local state.

Backend allows empty Authorization (only cookie). Cookie-based auth path was not exercised — only Bearer header was tested. /admin/login does not set httpOnly cookie (only returns JSON token), so cookie flow is currently unused for admin and that's consistent.
